chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa from Ibn Muskān from Sulayman ibn Khalid from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Witr prayer is three rak'ahs, separated between them, and in all of them is recited - 'Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad'.
ai.seo_question: How is the Witr prayer performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Witr prayer as a confirmed Sunnah consisting of three distinct rak'ahs, emphasizing the recitation of Surah Al-Ikhlas in each unit. The requirement to separate the rak'ahs (by sitting for Tashahhud) distinguishes this practice from the continuous prayer style, reflecting the juristic preference for maximizing acts of worship and remembrance. This specific mode of recitation highlights the centrality of divine unity (Tawhid) in the concluding prayers of the night.
